steps.description: Re-derived every headline over 255 completed schema-v4 sessions (the corpus grew from 245 since 2026-08-15) with four read-only instruments over committed artifacts; no new module. REPRODUCES: duration growth (trimmed OLS +0.966 min/day vs +0.947 claimed, R2 0.321 vs 0.307, Theil-Sen +0.909 vs +0.901, 29 of 255 excluded >240min). CORRECTIONS: (1) the 2.3x is NOT robust - it ranges 1.01x to 2.96x across defensible method choices, and under the spec's OWN named breakdown (the canonical four step keys) it is 1.01x, no rise at all. (2) The by-step-key attribution the spec asks for cannot be performed: the corpus holds 1,427 distinct completed step keys and the canonical four appear on a minority of sessions (register 91, cross-provider-verification 30, required-portion 27, close-out 9, of 255). (3) The instrumentation explanation is NOT ruled out: the count control the spec relies on misses the real artifact, which is timestamp dispersion - 44% of pre-cap completion intervals are under ONE SECOND (burst-logged) vs 34% post-cap, and burst logging mechanically deflates min/step; collapsing bursts at <=10s moves the ratio 2.65x -> 1.71x. (4) The flat-work control does not hold: work rose 5.96 -> 7.68 min/step (+29%), and +79% on the canonical classifier. (5) Model latency is 24% of the loop (8.0 of 33.5 min), not 11%. (6) Loop span is 33.5-35.8 min, not 41.7; the Step 8 tail is 12.6 min, not 17.9, and 8.1 of those 12.6 are recorded suite runtime. (7) The calendar trend does not survive into the measurable window: within the 57 round-ledger sessions the slope is +0.122 min/day, R2=0.000. NEW ATTRIBUTION, taxonomy-independent: a verification round costs +17.9 min of loop span (R2=0.625), of which only 3.3 min is model latency and 14.6 is not; 113 of 246 logged rounds (46%) are beyond the 2nd; remediation-review -> remediation-review is 62 transitions, median 18.1 min, 2,332 min (38.9 h) total, the largest single line item in the corpus; discovery -> supplementary is cheap at 4.6 min median. Recorded suite runtime is 18.6 min per instrumented session across 3 runs (pytest 9.53 median, playwright 6.65, mocha 0.62).

Dated every rise from first-row timestamps in the artifacts themselves. THE FINDING: the 2026-08-07 cohort split IS Set 111's landing date, and Set 111 built every instrument the post-cap cohort is measured with - sN-rounds.jsonl first row 2026-08-07 03:16 (bounds enforcement) and test-runs.jsonl first row 2026-08-07 15:40 (run_of_record + test_run_fresh). For those two ledgers the pre-cap cohort was not measured worse, it was not measured AT ALL, so the per-step comparison crosses an instrumented/uninstrumented boundary. Set 111 also shipped session_checklist, decision_journal, disposition.uat + uat_walk_recorded and spec_admission in the same window. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SPEC'S CANDIDATE LIST: (a) Set 128 is NOT the origin of the step skeleton - seeded plan-step rows first appear in Set 114 on 2026-08-10, two days before Set 128 ran; (b) Set 116 is a cost REDUCTION not a cause - it cut the suite ~3.6x via xdist and corrected published timings wrong by up to 30x, and raised the measured number only by making durationSeconds a required field on 2026-08-10. SLOWER vs MORE OBLIGATIONS, separated: no ceremony category acquired more steps (1.0 per session per category in BOTH cohorts). What moved is coverage - register 40%->98%, tests 42%->70% - which is instrumentation, not obligation. register is the clean case: coverage tripled while its per-step cost FELL 2.42 -> 0.80 min because start_session now logs it at the true moment. The one genuine new obligation is Set 111 S4's run-of-record, sized at 18.6 min/session.

Named the candidates with measured minutes, consequence and owner, and recorded the DISQUALIFIED ones with the measurement that disqualified them. C1 remediation round-trips: 62 remediation-review -> remediation-review transitions, median 18.1 min, 2,332 min (38.9 h) corpus, mean 33.8 min/session; marginal round cost +17.9 min of loop span (R2 0.625) of which only 3.3 min is model latency and 14.6 (82%) is not; consequence NONE if the same findings are fixed in fewer round-trips; owner orchestrator for fixing more per round, OPERATOR for anything that stops the loop earlier. Its real lever is Session 2's severity question. C2 recorded suite runtime: 18.6 min/session across 3 runs = 19% of the median session; consequence is a verification reduction; owner OPERATOR unconditionally, surfaced not proposed. DISQUALIFIED BY MEASUREMENT: C3 staleness-forced re-runs - only 13 runs / 67 minutes across the ENTIRE instrumented corpus had an unchanged surfaceDigest, 1.1 min/session mean and 0.0 median, so Sets 116 and 119 already closed it; C4 registration + close ceremony - 0.80 and 0.2 min/step, under 1.1 min/session combined, and register got 3x CHEAPER not more expensive; C5 discovery -> supplementary - 4.6 min median, the cheapest transition measured. C6 closing the stepKey vocabulary returns ZERO minutes so it does not go on the list; recorded as a measurement-integrity residual because 1,427 distinct keys are why the by-step-key breakdown could not be produced.

Phased loop, 3 rounds, closed within bounds (2 discovery passes and 2 remediation-review cycles permitted; 1 and 1 used). Verifier gpt-5.5 on openai; anthropic auto-excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider. Round 1 discovery, fan-out 2 (spec-conformance / failure-scenario lenses): ISSUES_FOUND, 1 blocking Major, 0 minor. Round 2 supplementary, run BEFORE any remediation as the loop requires: VERIFIED, zero findings, nothing joined the merge. THE FINDING, ACCEPTED WITHOUT ARGUMENT: the document drew operative conclusions from ai_router/router-metrics.jsonl, which git check-ignore confirms is ignored at .gitignore:7 and which git ls-files confirms is untracked - against a spec that requires analysis over committed artifacts only. The document had disclosed the file's machine-local status in section 6 while simultaneously promoting 'model latency 24% of the loop' into the section 5 list of values the rest of the set inherits; disclosure in a footnote does not cancel promotion in the inheritance list. Fixed by QUARANTINE not deletion, in four places (Method sources split committed vs machine-local; section 1 re-derived 'the lever is rounds not models' from the committed round cost alone; C1's latency row retitled NON-OPERATIVE and carrying the clause that C1's minutes are unchanged if it is struck; section 5 latency figure removed and replaced with an explicit prohibition). NO MEASURED MINUTES MOVED - every candidate number comes from sN-rounds.jsonl, test-runs.jsonl, activity-log.json and session-state.json, all committed. Consistency propagated to all three echoes in the same pass (G-012): s1-conventions.md edited, a CORRECTING record appended to decisions.jsonl via the sanctioned writer rather than editing the append-only journal, and the activity log correction carried here rather than by editing history. Acceptance harness round 1: 1 judgment-kind criterion, never auto-closed by design. Round 3 remediation-review over the fix delta: VERIFIED, 1 fix accepted / 0 rejected / 0 accepted-with-modification, zero new findings.

Nothing owed, and this is the gate's own answer rather than a judgement: `run_of_record affected` reports 'No declared suite's input set intersects this change (0 path(s))', re-run after remediation with the final change set. Every file this session touched is under docs/session-sets/134-ceremony-cost-and-what-to-cut/ - one analysis document, a conventions block, a remediation sidecar, the routed ai-assignment ledger, and machine-written lifecycle files. No ai_router path, no extension path, no test input set. Under the constitution a suite this session did not touch is not owed at all, so no run of record is produced and none is required by test_run_fresh. The four analysis instruments were written and run from the session workspace, never in the repo, so the set adds no module and no suite covers them.
